title: Responder Operations Manual: Synthesized Procedures and Communication Templates
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary

This document is a concise, operational manual for responders responsible for stabilizing Redwood Inference services during customer-impacting events. It synthesizes guidance across detection, triage, containment, stabilization, restoration, post-incident analysis, on-call rotations, and customer communications. The goal is fast, repeatable decision-making with clear accountability and artifact collection for downstream audits and postmortems.

Who should read this
- Primary: on-call responders and bridge operators (SRE, serving runtime, infra).
- Secondary: product incident liaisons, customer success leads, and engineering managers who will review postmortem artifacts.

Scope and goals
- Scope: production-facing degradations that affect latency, throughput, error rates, model quality regressions, or core control plane availability. Not a replacement for component-specific runbooks; see component runbook index for low-level commands.
- Goals: minimize customer-visible impact, preserve forensic evidence, communicate clearly, and generate a postmortem-ready artifact set.

Roles & responsibilities
- Bridge Operator (Bridge): runs the incident bridge, coordinates updates, and owns customer-facing cadence until handoff.
- Stabilizer: executes corrective actions (scaling, cache flushes, partial rollbacks) and reports progress.
- Escalation Owner: senior engineer who approves rollbacks, infra changes, or legal/security engagements.
- Scribe: records timeline, hypotheses tested, and telemetry snapshots.
- Customer Liaison: prepares and posts external status updates and coordinates with CS.

Incident lifecycle (high-level)
1) Detect: automated alert or customer report. Evidence: alert URL, example request IDs, and sample failing responses.
2) Acknowledge & Create Bridge: owner creates a bridge with subject line prefix: [STAB] <service> <symptom>.
3) Triage: classify severity, impact scope, and likely components (runtime, cache, control plane, network).
4) Contain: apply non-destructive mitigations to stop escalation (rate limit, circuit-break, disable integrations).
5) Stabilize: targeted fixes, Canary rollback, route traffic away, or scale capacity.
6) Recover: restore normal traffic patterns and monitor for regressions.
7) Post-effect: collect artifacts, runbook updates, and schedule postmortem.

Severity definitions and decision thresholds
- Sev3 (minor): small set of customers affected, degraded P95 latency > target by 2x for 5+ minutes.
- Sev2 (major): broad customer impact, error rate spike > 1% absolute or 5x baseline for 5+ minutes, or sustained P95 degradation > 3x.
- Sev1 (critical): total or near-total outage for a region or platform-wide control plane failure.

10-minute stabilization checklist (run immediately once bridge is up)
1) Bridge URL, pager owner, and short subject in bridge title.
2) Quick evidence capture: list 3 representative request IDs, link to alert, and paste CLI output for service status.
3) Short customer-facing statement: "We are investigating elevated errors/latency for <service>. Initial mitigation in progress."
4) Apply containment: incremental throttles, disable non-essential integrations, or move traffic to healthy pool.
5) Identify one tactical action to try next (scale, cache clear, rollback).

Decision matrix (text table)
Trigger | Immediate containment | Next action owner
"Error rate spike > 5x" | Activate per-tenant throttles; enable degraded-mode | Stabilizer
"KV cache hot miss storm" | Reduce TTLs; promote healthy cache nodes | Stabilizer
"Model quality regression (high hallucination)" | Route to validated fallback model; pause model rollout | Escalation Owner

Escalation ladder (contact sequence)
1) On-call responder (primary pager)
2) Service lead (phone)
3) Platform SRE lead (if >15 minutes without stabilization)
4) CTO/VP Eng (for Sev1 or sustained outage >60 minutes)

Customer-facing status templates
- Initial (first 15 minutes):
Subject: Service degradation for <service> — investigating
Body: We are investigating elevated errors/latency affecting <service> in <region>. Engineers are actively working on mitigation. We will post an update within 15 minutes.

- Update (progress):
Subject: Update: <service> degradation — partial mitigation in place
Body: We implemented <mitigation>. Error rate reduced from X% to Y%. Some customers may still see intermittent issues. ETA for full restoration: ~30 minutes.

- Resolution:
Subject: Resolved: <service> — normal operation restored
Body: The issue impacting <service> has been resolved as of <timestamp UTC>. Root cause analysis is underway; we will follow up with a postmortem. If you continue to see issues please reply to this message or open a support ticket.

- Follow-up postmortem notice:
Subject: Postmortem scheduled for <service> incident on <date>
Body: We will publish the postmortem by <date>. Action items and mitigation plan will be included.

Evidence & artifact checklist (required for all Sev2/Sev1)
- Alert URL(s) and timestamps
- Representative request IDs and full request/response payloads (redact PII)
- Dashboard links pinned to the bridge
- Core dump/log bundles or AWS/GCP diagnostic snapshots
- A list of commands executed (with timestamps) and the person who ran them

Minimum runbook fragments to attach for common faults
- High error rate:
  - Commands: "kubectl get pods -n serving"; "rds-cli describe-connections --filter service=<service>"
  - Dashboards: Serving P95 latency, error-rate by model, recent deploys table
- Cache storm:
  - Commands: "redis-cli INFO"; "prometheus query: sum(rate(redis_command_duration_seconds_count[1m])) by (instance)"
  - Short fix: "Increase read-replicas; evict largest keys carefully using ITERATE/EVICT script"
- Model quality regression:
  - Commands: "rollout manager rollback --model <id> --to-version <prior>"; add telemetry for model-score drift

Postmortem & follow-up process
- Timeline: publish draft within 72 hours; final postmortem and action item list within 10 business days.
- Required sections: Summary, Impact, Root cause, Timeline of decisions, Mitigations applied, Corrective actions (owner + ETA), Detection gap, Preventative measures.
- Severity review committee: for Sev1 incidents, at least one SRE, one product manager, and one CS lead must review the draft.

On-call rotation guidance and handoff checklist
- Rotation length: typical 7 days for primary responder, 14 days for supporting buckets.
- Shadowing: new responders shadow for 2 full rotations before independently owning critical bridges.
- Handoff checklist (to be run at shift change):
  1) Confirm no active bridges or escalate if unresolved.
 2) Share list of outstanding action items (owner + ETA).
 3) Provide any live tickets or ongoing communications with customers.
 4) Confirm monitoring subscriptions and pager escalation targets.

Game day recipes (low-overhead exercises teams can run monthly)
- KV cache eviction storm: simulate cache thrash against staging cluster, practice containment (throttle, promote replicas). Success criteria: restore P95 within 20 minutes without full restart.
- Canary model rollback: rollout a model with injected bad responses, validate rollback steps and customer routing. Success criteria: rollback completes and no customer requests hit faulty model after 10 minutes.
- Rate-limit cascade: artificially apply a tenant-level throttle and verify upstream controllers obey circuit-breakers and SLOs. Success criteria: no global outage; automated alerts produce a useful signal.

Evidence collection SOP for audits and enterprise customers
1) Export dashboards as PNG and CSV and upload to bridge notes immediately.
2) Attach zipped log bundle with a README of time windows used.
3) Sanitize customer data using the sanitization script: "scripts/sanitize-logs --from <t1> --to <t2> --redact-keys email,ssn"

Maintenance windows and restoration cadence (policy)
- Rolling maintenance: prefer rolling capacity upgrades with live health checks.
- Forced restoration windows: for customer-impacting fixes that require downtime, coordinate with CS and give minimum 72 hours notice for enterprise customers.

Appendix: sample internal bridge transcript template
- Header: Bridge URL, Incident ID, Severity, Initial symptom
- Timeline entries: timestamp | actor | action | result | evidence link
  - Example: 2026-02-05T15:12Z | Maya Chen | scaled serving pool +20% | P95 reduced 35% | link to dashboard

Appendix: quick commands and common dashboards (copy-paste)
- Get serving pods: kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving -o wide
- Check autoscaler: redwoodctl autoscale status --service <service>
- Prometheus query: sum(rate(http_server_errors_total[1m])) by (service)

Related resources and ownership
- Component runbook index: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/index
- SLO & escalation policy: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets-2025
- Playbook maintenance: owners of this document should review after every Sev2/Sev1 and update within 7 days.

End of document
